blocks.content:
Citizenship refers to the legal relationship between an individual and the State. A citizen enjoys full civil and political rights such as the right to vote, hold public office, and protection under law.

Non-citizens do not enjoy political rights.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Citizenship represents the legal relationship binding an individual to the State.
Citizens possess full civil and political rights, including the right to vote and hold public office.
Non-citizens are excluded from enjoying political rights.
India adopts a single citizenship model, meaning there is no distinct state citizenship.
The single citizenship system in India is specifically designed to strengthen national unity.
India enforces Single Citizenship only; there is no provision for state-level citizenship.
Non-citizens do not enjoy political rights such as voting or holding public office in India.
Contrast between Indian (Single Citizenship) and USA (Dual Citizenship) systems is a frequently tested topic.

blocks.content:
India follows the concept of single citizenship.

This means:
• There is only Indian citizenship.
• There is no separate state citizenship.

This feature strengthens national unity.

In contrast, countries like the USA follow dual citizenship.
